standard_prerequisites.name: Torsion complexes and their reduction to sheaves
standard_prerequisites.statement: A complex K in D^+(X_etale) with torsion cohomology sheaves can be represented by a bounded below complex of torsion abelian sheaves (Cohomology on Sites, declared as a tagged source pointer).
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the reduction at source lines 1977-1981.

standard_prerequisites.name: Leray's acyclicity lemma
standard_prerequisites.statement: If a complex is acyclic for the higher direct images of the functor, then the higher direct images of the complex vanish in positive degrees (Derived Categories, declared as a tagged source pointer).
standard_prerequisites.use: It finishes the complex case at source lines 1985-1988.

standard_prerequisites.name: The comparison lemma for the ph topology
standard_prerequisites.statement: a_{X,*}a_X^{-1}F = F and R^i epsilon_{X,*}(a_X^{-1}F) = 0 for i > 0 for torsion F (the author's lemma-comparison-ph-etale, retained as context).
standard_prerequisites.use: It gives the identity and one vanishing at source lines 1992-1999.

standard_prerequisites.name: Descent along the projection to the small etale site
standard_prerequisites.statement: R^j pi_{X,*}(pi_X^{-1}F) = 0 for j > 0 (the author's lemma-cohomological-descent-etale, retained as context).
standard_prerequisites.use: It supplies the other vanishing in the Leray decomposition at source lines 2002-2003.

standard_prerequisites.name: The relative Leray spectral sequence
standard_prerequisites.statement: The Leray spectral sequence for a composite functor, used for a_X = epsilon_X o pi_X (Cohomology on Sites, declared as a tagged source pointer).
standard_prerequisites.use: It combines the two vanishing statements at source lines 1995-1997.

core_obligations: Reduce to a single torsion abelian sheaf: represent K by a bounded below complex of torsion sheaves, apply the sheaf case degreewise and Leray's acyclicity lemma (source lines 1977-1989).
Sheaf case, first identity: a_{X,*}a_X^{-1}F = F is the second part of the chapter's comparison lemma (source lines 1991-1994).

Sheaf case, vanishing: decompose a_X as epsilon_X o pi_X, use the relative Leray spectral sequence, the vanishing R^i epsilon_{X,*}(a_X^{-1}F) = 0 from the comparison lemma, and the vanishing R^j pi_{X,*}(pi_X^{-1}F) = 0 from the descent lemma (source lines 1994-2003).

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce the complex case to one torsion abelian sheaf, using the torsion representation and Leray's acyclicity lemma.
Use the comparison lemma for the identity a_{X,*}a_X^{-1}F = F and reduce to the vanishing.
Combine the relative Leray spectral sequence with the two vanishing statements for epsilon_{X,*} and pi_{X,*}.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-cohomological-descent-etale-ph at source lines 1962-1973: for K in D^+(X_etale) with torsion cohomology sheaves the maps pi_X^{-1}K -> R epsilon_{X,*}a_X^{-1}K and K -> R a_{X,*}a_X^{-1}K are isomorphisms. The author's proof at source lines 1975-2005 proves the second statement only (noting the first is easier and identical in method), first reducing from a bounded below complex of torsion sheaves to the case of a single torsion abelian sheaf by representing K by such a complex (a cross-chapter pointer) and applying Leray's acyclicity lemma (a second pointer) to the case of one sheaf, and then proving that case from the two parts of the chapter's comparison lemma (retained as context) together with the relative Leray spectral sequence for a_X = epsilon_X o pi_X, the vanishing of the higher direct images of epsilon_{X,*} on a_X^{-1}F, and the vanishing of R^j pi_{X,*} on pi_X^{-1}F supplied by the chapter's descent lemma (also retained as context). The counted argument is therefore a complete two-stage reduction whose in-chapter ingredients are all available inside the package.
